newsitem.title: USA: Workers remove fuel from grounded barge.
newsitem.headline: Workers remove fuel from grounded barge.

text.p: Emergency crews were working Monday to offload diesel fuel from a barge grounded in southwestern Alaska's Togiak Bay, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

The Boxer, owned by Seattle-based Northcoast Fisheries Seafood Processors Inc., broke free of its mooring during stormy weather Thursday, the Coast Guard said. Efforts to remove the 50,000 gallons of diesel fuel on board the ship have been hampered by continued bad weather, the Coast Guard said.
No one was injured in the mishap, and there is no evidence of any fuel spill, said Coast Guard spokesman Tod Lyons.

A company hired by the Boxer's owner began lightering operations Sunday, but had to stop because of bad weather, Lyons said. Workers were able to resume Monday afternoon, when weather calmed, he said.
"It looks like they're going to be able to remove all or most of the fuel that's on board sometime today," Lyons said.
The Coast Guard, which was overseeing the operation, was concerned about possible spills from the disabled vessel, he said.
The grounded barge, stuck in a listing position, has been surrounded by oil-containment booms in case any fuel spills, and two oil-collecting skimmer vessels were standing by, the Coast Guard said.
The Boxer was functioning as a supply and storage site for other fishing vessels in the area, Lyons siad.
